# 🚨 edstem-cli 0.8.2: security release

> [!CAUTION]
> **🔴 Self-hosting the remote MCP server? Upgrade and redeploy today.**
> On 0.8.0 and earlier, one oversized request to `/mcp` can exhaust the server's memory and take it down ([GHSA-46jr-4wx8-v453](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-46jr-4wx8-v453), high). If OAuth is **off**, anyone who can reach the server can send that request. No token is needed.

```bash
npm install -g edstem-cli@0.8.2
```

Docker users: pull the new image and restart the container. Worker users: run `wrangler deploy` again from 0.8.2.

## 👥 Who needs to act

| | You run | Risk on ≤ 0.8.0 | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 🔴 | **A self-hosted remote server, OAuth off** | Anyone can crash it with a single request | **Upgrade now** |
| 🟠 | A self-hosted remote server with OAuth, or your own Worker | Any holder of a valid token can crash it | **Upgrade now** |
| 🟡 | The local CLI or stdio `edstem-mcp` | Not exposed: the bug is HTTP-only | Upgrade at your next update |
| 🟢 | The hosted server `edstem.tuuhub.com` | Already patched and redeployed | Nothing |

✅ No compromised or malicious package was involved. These are upstream bugs, already fixed upstream. 0.8.2 closes every advisory `npm audit` reported against 0.8.0 (18 packages: 3 critical, 11 high, 4 moderate). It includes the 0.8.1 fixes, and `edstem update` now compares against the version you are running. Commands and MCP tools behave as before.

## 🛡️ Runtime fixes

| Package | Change | Advisory | Reachable in edstem-cli? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@modelcontextprotocol/server`, `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` | 2.0.0 → 2.3.1, 1.30.0 → 1.32.1 | [GHSA-46jr-4wx8-v453](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-46jr-4wx8-v453) (high): one request within the default size limit exhausts memory during validation | 🔴 **Yes**, on the remote HTTP server |
| | | [GHSA-jm63-cq47-j5jp](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jm63-cq47-j5jp) (high): a shared server instance delivers one client's messages to another | ⚪ No. Each request gets a new server instance |
| | | [GHSA-rvq5-wwqv-78pq](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rvq5-wwqv-78pq) (high): the SDK's bearer middleware accepts tokens issued for another service | ⚪ No. edstem verifies tokens with its own provider |
| | | [GHSA-6qxp-vccf-f47h](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6qxp-vccf-f47h), [GHSA-6prh-2h8m-c8cw](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6prh-2h8m-c8cw) (high): the OAuth client leaks credentials to another origin | ⚪ No. These are client-side bugs, and edstem is a server |
| | | [GHSA-22jm-h49p-29qw](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-22jm-h49p-29qw) (high): experimental tasks are not bound to their session | ⚪ No. Tasks are not used |
| `agents` | 0.20.1 → 0.29.0 | Pulls in the fixed SDK above | 🔴 Yes, it is part of the Worker |
| `fast-uri` (via `ajv`) | 3.1.6 → 3.1.9 | [GHSA-qw65-cvwx-89v3](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qw65-cvwx-89v3), [GHSA-58mr-gqgx-xq4g](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-58mr-gqgx-xq4g), [GHSA-hrr3-gc8f-f4qj](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-hrr3-gc8f-f4qj) (high): host confusion when parsing URIs | 🟡 Unlikely. edstem does not route requests by ajv-validated URIs |
| `proxy-addr`, `qs`, `ip-address`, `hono` (via the SDK) | patched | [GHSA-jqcg-44mw-7w3h](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jqcg-44mw-7w3h) (critical, IP spoofing), plus qs DoS, ip-address SSRF classification, and hono parser bugs | ⚪ No. edstem serves HTTP through its own fetch handlers and never mounts the SDK's Express or Hono servers |

## 🧰 Development-only fixes

These packages ship in neither the npm package nor the Worker. They affect only contributors who run the test suite or `wrangler dev`.

- `vitest` 3.2.7 → 5.0.5: closes the tinypool prototype-pollution-to-RCE gadgets ([GHSA-5gmw-xhrv-c9v3](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5gmw-xhrv-c9v3), [GHSA-85c8-ppgw-ccpr](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-85c8-ppgw-ccpr), critical) and `@vitest/mocker` arbitrary file read and code injection.
- `vite` 7.3.6 → 8.x: dev-server cross-origin script execution and `server.fs.allow` bypass.
- `wrangler` 4.118.0 → 4.151.3: the bundled `undici` (15 advisories, including TLS validation bypass and cross-user cookie disclosure) and `sharp` (libheif and librsvg CVEs).
- `source-map-js` 1.2.1 → 1.2.2: denial of service through crafted source maps.

⚙️ Use Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1, or 26.12.1, or a newer supported security patch.
